records.description: The reviewed KamLAND reactor disappearance, SNO active-flavor transformation, Super-Kamiokande atmospheric disappearance and OPERA accelerator tau-appearance results support flavor change compatible with their declared oscillation models across different preparations and responses. Their counts, fluxes, averaged probabilities and conditional fit parameters are distinct observables. This synthesis preserves those boundaries and supplies neither a pooled transition probability nor a new global fit.
records.name: Neutrino oscillation evidence across preparations
openObligations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

limitations: This is a literature synthesis of already admitted results. Each chain retains its acquisition, selection, adopted flux/cross sections, detector response, backgrounds and inference contexts. Counts are not event-level oscillation probabilities. Reused events, multiple summaries and alternative fits within an acquisition are dependent; this synthesis is not another independent experiment or combined significance.

KamLAND reactor antineutrinos involve changing reactor histories and baselines. The reported period-averaged survival and historical two-flavor rate-and-shape fit use response and background models; the 180 km display baseline is not a single experimental baseline. Shape-only, KamLAND-only and solar-combined fits are distinct, and the solar combination adds a CPT assumption.

SNO reports a joint electron versus combined muon-plus-tau active-flux inference under its B8-shape and weak-response assumptions. This is not a measured oscillation phase, separate muon/tau identification or unique proof of adiabatic MSW conversion. Subtracting channel-flux centers does not reproduce its covariance, joint result or significance; the SK-added and shape-relaxed analyses remain separate.

Super-Kamiokande uses atmospheric flux, zenith distributions and detector/kinematic proxies with a historical two-flavor fit. The 1998 disappearance analysis does not directly identify tau appearance or distinguish its tau interpretation from the stated sterile alternative. Its L/E cross-check reuses the sample and does not resolve an oscillation dip.

OPERA reconstructs tau candidates in a primarily muon-neutrino beam using channel-dependent efficiencies and backgrounds. Its calibrated channel-combination significance, signal strength and full-mixing mass-squared compatibility reuse the same candidate sample. Dividing five candidates by an interaction total does not produce an oscillation probability, and the Fisher-product statistic is not the calibrated tail probability.

Historical effective two-flavor parameters, confidence constructions and adopted external inputs retain their publication-specific meanings; no current three-flavor global fit is inferred. These results do not establish absolute neutrino masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac/Majorana character, a unique mass-generation mechanism or quantitative astrophysical/cosmological transport.

Flavor and mass labels are bases, not distinct classical populations measured simultaneously. Minimal massless Standard Model field assignments do not generate the mass extension.

The plane-wave, coherent, ultrarelativistic vacuum approximation uses hbar=c=1. An experiment averages with flux, cross section, efficiency and resolution; a single vacuum phase is not a detector likelihood. Oscillation differences do not determine absolute masses, every individual mass to be nonzero, Dirac versus Majorana character or a unique mass-generation mechanism. Matter propagation and solar, atmospheric and accelerator acquisitions remain outside this finite reactor block.

rationale.scope: Declared coherent neutrino mixing and the KamLAND 2002-2004 reactor acquisition; no universal mass-generation or formation rule.
rationale.statement: In the coherent ultrarelativistic vacuum approximation with hbar=c=1, A_alpha-to-beta=sum_i U_beta,i exp[-i m_i^2 L/(2E)] U_alpha,i* and P=|A|^2. Antineutrinos replace U by U*. With v_g=(v_gi+v_gk)/2 and nonzero Delta v_g=|v_gi-v_gk|, l_coh approximately v_g sigma_x/Delta v_g is a separation scale: L << l_coh leaves that overlap unsuppressed, while substantial separation suppresses its interference term. records.name: Neutrino wave-packet overlap
openObligations: The approximation linearizes the dispersion relation over a narrow momentum distribution and neglects packet spreading. The characteristic length is shape-dependent, not an exact universal damping law or sharp boundary; equal group velocities produce no separation by this mechanism.

A source-only packet width is insufficient. A sufficiently coherent detection process can allow separated emitted components to interfere; the effective overlap already incorporates this condition, not an ordinary detector energy-bin width.

Loss of a local interference term does not establish fundamental nonunitarity, collapse, absorption or neutrino decay. Propagation through varying matter, scattering and environmental dynamics require separately specified evolution and are not derived here.
